benchmark.title: Levels 1–9 foundations-to-AI benchmark
benchmark.sourceBoundary: A line-by-line index of the learner-supplied inventory's Master/Study targets and explicit Level-2 AI-research additions. It preserves target wording and source-line locations, maps each target to an Atlas target, and excludes the inventory's reading lists. This calibration never claims current delivery, learner completion, or verified mastery.

extensionTracks.title: Mathematical, Algorithms & Theory Deepening

cadence.rationale: Theory needs spaced proof reconstruction, counterexamples, and one revised argument—not a single compressed survey.

extensionTracks.project: Prove, stress-test, and explain one advanced algorithm, theorem, or numerical/optimization claim with an explicit assumption ledger.
extensionTracks.oralDefense: Defend the model, quantifiers, reduction or derivation, counterexample, and the boundary between proof and experiment.
extensionTracks.nonClaim: Design-only extension; it does not represent a full mathematics/theory degree sequence, credit, or research qualification.

extensionTracks.title: Deep Learning & ML Systems

cadence.rationale: Repeatable experiments need time to inspect systems evidence, revise the baseline, and explain resource and reliability limits.

extensionTracks.project: Reproduce one bounded training/inference result with versioned data, metrics, resource observations, and a meaningful baseline.
extensionTracks.oralDefense: Explain the computation graph, optimization choices, system bottleneck, generalization limits, and rollback/monitoring plan.
extensionTracks.nonClaim: No GPU performance, framework fluency, distributed-scale capability, or production reliability is implied until directly observed.

extensionTracks.title: Probabilistic Modeling, Sequential Decision-Making & RL

cadence.rationale: Inference and decision claims need a separate calibration and revision cycle so a finite simulation is not mistaken for a policy guarantee.

extensionTracks.project: Build and compare a bounded inference or decision model with held-out evidence, uncertainty calibration, and explicit reward/utility assumptions.
extensionTracks.oralDefense: Trace an inference or Bellman claim, change one observation/reward premise, and state what becomes unknown or unsafe to automate.
extensionTracks.nonClaim: No general decision policy, control guarantee, safe RL claim, or real-world deployment authority follows from a bounded exercise.

extensionTracks.title: Foundation Models, Generative AI & NLP

cadence.rationale: Model and data provenance, evaluation, red-teaming, and human-override reasoning need revision after the first dossier.

extensionTracks.project: Create one bounded language/model evaluation dossier that joins token/data provenance, task metric, retrieval or tool boundary, red team, and human override.
extensionTracks.oralDefense: Use a readable whiteboard to explain a model/data/evaluation trace, an adversarial or changed-premise failure, and the next falsifier.
extensionTracks.nonClaim: No claim of LLM training, alignment, mechanistic interpretability, model security, or NLP research specialization is made without direct project evidence.

phases.title: Execution, claims, and discrete structure
phases.premise: Before a system can be designed or optimized, model state and make claims precise enough to prove or refute.
phases.gate: Defend one invariant, repair one flawed proof, construct a smallest counterexample, and name the cost model of the check.

phases.title: Representation and algorithmic strategy
phases.premise: A representation decides which operations are cheap, which invariants are local, and which strategy the structure permits.
phases.gate: Read an unfamiliar data-structure implementation, recover its invariant, compare strategies, and defend a cost/evidence boundary.

phases.title: Durable software and shared data
phases.premise: Local algorithms become useful when contracts, tests, artifacts, and transactions preserve meaning over time.
phases.gate: Trace a claim through an interface, test, and data boundary; diagnose one failed change; defend a repair with regression evidence.

phases.title: Execution, numerical models, and evidence
phases.premise: Machine behavior, linear structure, continuous change, uncertainty, and optimization explain what a numerical or ML claim can mean.
phases.gate: Derive a projection or likelihood step, name a numerical/data assumption, reject an overclaim, and explain what evidence would change it.

phases.title: Machine, network, and runtime boundaries
phases.premise: Applications live inside machines, processes, schedules, networks, and trust boundaries; each changes what can be known.
phases.gate: Read a trace across system layers, name an ownership/failure boundary, and reject a claim the observation cannot establish.

phases.title: Formal theory, classical AI, and learning
phases.premise: AI joins language, search, decision, representation, statistics, execution limits, and evidence rather than a single model call.
phases.gate: Model a problem before selecting an algorithm or model; identify an assumption, data boundary, and transfer risk.

phases.title: Evidence and human control
phases.premise: A model or agent is useful only when its assumptions, authority, feedback, and uncertainty remain inspectable and challengeable.
phases.gate: Produce an evidence-and-human-control packet naming the claim, limitation, owner, and next falsifier.

phases.title: Capstone release and oral architecture defense
phases.premise: A maintained release must connect mathematical argument, implementation evidence, tests, security, human impact, and revisable decisions.
phases.gate: Defend a versioned evidence bundle: claim, trace, test/observation, human impact, limitation, rollback, and next reason to revise.
